title: A memory map
description:
Read a process memory map and say where an address lives.

```
0x00400000-0x00401000 r-xp game          -> code of the main program
0x7f12a0000000-0x7f12a0021000 rw-p [heap]
address 0x400123 -> game (r-x), offset 0x123
address 0x1000 -> not mapped
```
hints: `std::upper_bound` on `start` and stepping back one finds the candidate region; then check `address < end`.
requirements: Parse lines in the Linux `/proc/self/maps` format (start-end, permissions, and a name).
Look up an address with a binary search over sorted regions.
Print the permissions in words (readable, writable, executable).
stretch: On Windows, build the same list for your own process with `VirtualQuery` in a loop.
